---
title: "Topology Checker"
date: 2026-09-03
categories: [tool, geometry]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and check it for the five recurring topology errors — overlap, gap, sliver, duplicates, dangle. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether any
feature overlaps, leaves a gap, is a sliver, duplicates another, or
(for lines) dangles unconnected.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

This is diagnosis only, not repair — fixing a topology error almost
always requires a human decision (see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for why), so there's no
"Fix" step here, just the report and a map to inspect it on.

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using GeoPandas/Shapely underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained one check at a time.

Gap and sliver aren't absolute properties of a dataset — they depend
on a judgment call. **Sliver threshold** (compactness, 0-1): how thin
counts as "not a real shape" — lower catches only thinner slivers.
**Gap search distance** (degrees): how close two features need to be
before a gap between them counts — larger finds gaps further apart.

```{.webgeods-python #topology-diagnose-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
#| inject: [sliverThreshold, gapProximity]
import math
from shapely.geometry import mapping, shape

def geom_family(gdf):
    types = set(gdf.geometry.geom_type)
    if types <= {"Polygon", "MultiPolygon"}:
        return "polygon"
    if types <= {"LineString", "MultiLineString"}:
        return "line"
    if types <= {"Point", "MultiPoint"}:
        return "point"
    return "mixed"

def check_overlap(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                area = gi.intersection(gj).area
                results[i].append(("overlap", j, area))
                results[j].append(("overlap", i, area))
    return results

def check_duplicate(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if gdf.geometry.iloc[i].equals(gdf.geometry.iloc[j]):
                results[i].append(("duplicate", j, 0))
                results[j].append(("duplicate", i, 0))
    return results

def check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=0.15):
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        perim = geom.length
        area = geom.area
        if perim > 0:
            compactness = 4 * math.pi * area / (perim ** 2)
            if compactness < compactness_threshold:
                results[i].append(("sliver", None, compactness))
    return results

def check_gap(gdf, min_area=1e-6, proximity=0.06):
    n = len(gdf)
    gaps = []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                continue
            if gi.equals(gj):
                continue
            if gi.distance(gj) > proximity:
                continue
            pair_union = gi.union(gj)
            gap_geom = pair_union.convex_hull.difference(pair_union)
            if not gap_geom.is_empty:
                parts = gap_geom.geoms if hasattr(gap_geom, "geoms") else [gap_geom]
                for part in parts:
                    if part.area > min_area:
                        gaps.append(part)
    return gaps

def check_dangle(gdf, tolerance=1e-9):
    endpoints = []
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        coords = list(geom.coords)
        endpoints.append((i, "start", coords[0]))
        endpoints.append((i, "end", coords[-1]))
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, which, (x, y) in endpoints:
        connected = False
        for j, which2, (x2, y2) in endpoints:
            if j == i:
                continue
            if ((x - x2) ** 2 + (y - y2) ** 2) ** 0.5 <= tolerance:
                connected = True
                break
        if not connected:
            results[i].append(("dangle", which, 0))
    return results

def detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=0.15, gap_proximity=0.06):
    family = geom_family(gdf)
    n = len(gdf)
    per_feature = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    extra_features = []

    dup = check_duplicate(gdf)
    for i in range(n):
        per_feature[i].extend(dup[i])

    if family == "polygon":
        ov = check_overlap(gdf)
        sl = check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=sliver_threshold)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(ov[i])
            per_feature[i].extend(sl[i])
        for gap_geom in check_gap(gdf, proximity=gap_proximity):
            extra_features.append({
                "type": "Feature",
                "properties": {
                    "name": "gap", "error_type": "gap", "has_error": True,
                    "partner": "", "metric": round(gap_geom.area, 6), "severity": "warning"
                },
                "geometry": mapping(gap_geom)
            })
    elif family == "line":
        dg = check_dangle(gdf)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(dg[i])

    names = gdf["name"] if "name" in gdf.columns else [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(n)]
    features = []
    for i in range(n):
        errs = per_feature[i]
        has_error = len(errs) > 0
        error_type = errs[0][0] if has_error else ""
        partner_idx = errs[0][1] if has_error and isinstance(errs[0][1], int) else None
        partner = str(names.iloc[partner_idx] if hasattr(names, "iloc") else names[partner_idx]) if partner_idx is not None else ""
        metric = round(errs[0][2], 6) if has_error else 0
        features.append({
            "type": "Feature",
            "properties": {
                "name": names.iloc[i] if hasattr(names, "iloc") else names[i],
                "error_type": error_type, "has_error": has_error,
                "partner": partner, "metric": metric,
                "severity": "error" if has_error else ""
            },
            "geometry": mapping(gdf.geometry.iloc[i])
        })
    features.extend(extra_features)
    return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}

import geopandas as gpd

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

if gdf is not None and "name" not in gdf.columns:
    gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

if gdf is None:
    a = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.45, 41.85], [12.52, 41.85], [12.52, 41.92], [12.45, 41.92], [12.45, 41.85]]]}
    b = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.50, 41.87], [12.57, 41.87], [12.57, 41.94], [12.50, 41.94], [12.50, 41.87]]]}
    gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame({"name": ["A (example)", "B (example)"]}, geometry=[shape(a), shape(b)], crs="EPSG:4326")

detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=sliverThreshold, gap_proximity=gapProximity)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
checkButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.textContent = "▶ Check";
  button.onclick = async () => {
    button.disabled = true;
    button.classList.add("webgeods-btn-loading");
    button.textContent = "⌛ Checking...";
    try {
      // #| inject reads window[name] fresh on every run() — see the
      // hidden cell's pragma line. Read straight from the slider
      // elements (not the OJS sliverControl/gapControl cell values)
      // so this button's own cell stays independent of the sliders:
      // referencing an OJS variable by name here would make OJS
      // re-create this whole button on every drag tick.
      window.sliverThreshold = +document.getElementById("sliver-threshold-control").value;
      window.gapProximity = +document.getElementById("gap-proximity-control").value;
      await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("topology-diagnose-py").run();
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
      button.classList.remove("webgeods-btn-loading");
      button.textContent = "▶ Check";
    }
  };
  return button;
}
```

*First run loads the Python engine — expect 30-40 seconds. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The color is decided by JS, not Python — see topology-errors.qmd for
// the full explanation. The geometry type isn't fixed (polygons for
// overlap/gap/sliver/duplicates, lines for dangle), so the paint
// itself depends on the data: setGeoJSON() (shared/map.js) detects on
// its own when the layer's TYPE needs to change and recreates it.
errorPaint = (data) => {
  const geometryType = data?.features?.find((f) => f?.geometry?.type)?.geometry?.type ?? "";
  const colorExpr = ["case", ["==", ["get", "has_error"], true], "#e05252", "#3d5a73"];
  if (geometryType === "LineString" || geometryType === "MultiLineString") {
    return { "line-color": colorExpr, "line-width": 4 };
  }
  if (geometryType === "Point" || geometryType === "MultiPoint") {
    return { "circle-color": colorExpr, "circle-radius": 6 };
  }
  return { "fill-color": colorExpr, "fill-opacity": 0.55 };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
```
```{ojs}
topologyStats = Generators.observe((change) => {
  const compute = () => {
    const features = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("topology-py")?.features ?? [];
    const total = features.length;
    const errors = features.filter((f) => f.properties?.has_error === true).length;
    change({ total, errors });
  };
  compute();
  const handler = (e) => {
    if (e.dataType === "source" && e.sourceDataType === "content" && e.sourceId === "topology-py") {
      compute();
    }
  };
  sharedMap.map.on("sourcedata", handler);
  return () => sharedMap.map.off("sourcedata", handler);
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
// Not promoted to shared/ (still only one other tool using it, the
// Validator, with a slightly different call site): a Blob + a
// temporary <a download> is enough, no library needed.
downloadGeoJSON = (sourceId, filename) => {
  const data = sharedMap.getGeoJSON(sourceId);
  if (!data) return;
  window.WebGeoDS.track?.("download_clicked", { tool: "topology-checker", sourceId });
  const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)], { type: "application/geo+json" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  a.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
```

```{ojs}

}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// One DOM node grouping Check/Download/Reset + the live status, built
// in JS rather than composed with several `${...}` markdown
// interpolations side by side — Pandoc's math-dollar parser reads
// adjacent `${x} ${y}` in the same paragraph as inline math and
// swallows them (see geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd, where this was
// actually hit). A single `${controlPanelRow}` avoids the ambiguity.
controlPanelRow = {
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.className = "webgeods-panel-row";
  row.append(checkButton, downloadButton, resetMapButton);
  const status = document.createElement("span");
  status.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
  status.textContent = `${topologyStats.total} feature, ${topologyStats.errors} with an error`;
  row.appendChild(status);
  return row;
}
```
